identification.summary: 1937CN is a China-linked group that Bkav, a Vietnamese security firm, believed was behind a wave of spyware intrusions into Vietnamese organizations from mid-2016, including the 29 July 2016 compromise of Vietnam Airlines' website and airport display and speaker systems [S4][S6]. Trend Micro (2023) assesses that its cluster Earth Zhulong is likely related to 1937CN, based on similar shellcode-loader code and overlapping victims [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: Bkav reported detecting the spyware in Vietnamese networks in mid-2012 [S7]. The earliest dated 1937CN-attributed event in the sources gathered is the late-June 2016 wave of intrusions [S4]. The imported record's claim of activity since 2013 is not confirmed by the sources gathered.
identification.notes: The 1937CN name comes from a self-styled Chinese group; press reports say it neither confirmed nor denied the 2016 airport attack, and one headline says it denied involvement [S5]. Trend Micro tracks Earth Zhulong as a separate vendor cluster that is only 'likely related' to 1937CN [S1]. Do not merge the 2016 Bkav-attributed activity with Earth Zhulong activity. No Microsoft actor name was found for this group.

attribution.confidence: Bkav stated the 2016 hackers were 'believed to be' members of 1937cn [S4]. Trend Micro describes Earth Zhulong as 'likely related' to 1937CN [S1]. No government attribution to a state sponsor was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Bkav: stolen data was sent to a lookalike domain of the Communist Party of Vietnam website (xxx.dcsvn.org) [S4]. Trend Micro: similar shellcode-loader code and overlapping victimology [S1][S2]. Vietnamese authorities and media blamed the group for the airport incident [S5][S6].

sectors: Telecommunications, technology and media (Earth Zhulong, 2020 onward)
regions: Southeast Asia (Trend Micro revised its Earth Zhulong report title to Southeast Asian firms) [S2]
targeting.notes: Bkav said the spyware compromised Vietnam Airlines and many other state organizations, businesses, banks, research institutes and universities [S4]. The July 2016 airport and airline incident carried messages about the South China Sea dispute [S6]. Telecom, technology and media targeting since 2020 is Trend Micro's finding for Earth Zhulong, not directly for 1937CN [S1][S3].

capabilities.summary: 2016 activity: Bkav described spyware that disguised itself as antivirus software, collected accounts and passwords, and received remote commands from the attacker; stolen data went to victim-specific subdomains of a spoofed Communist Party of Vietnam domain [S4]. Earth Zhulong (likely related): lure documents with malicious macros injecting Cobalt Strike shellcode, a custom ShellFang loader (three variants, 2020 to 2022, the latest with exception-based execution obfuscation and API hashing), and in early 2022 Group Policy Object abuse to deploy loaders and Cobalt Strike [S2][S3]. Cymulate also lists SharpHound, EarthWorm and Macamax among its tools [S3].

campaigns.name: Spyware first detected in Vietnamese networks
campaigns.summary: Bkav said it first detected the spyware in Vietnam's computer networks in mid-2012 and warned agencies, banks, institutes and universities several times afterward. Bkav's later link of this malware to 1937CN is its own assessment [S7][S4].

campaigns.name: Spyware wave against Vietnamese organizations
campaigns.summary: Bkav traced attacks on Vietnamese websites from late June 2016 to a spoofed Communist Party domain and said the hackers were believed to be 1937cn members [S4].

campaigns.name: Vietnam Airlines and airport compromise
campaigns.summary: Flight information screens and speakers at Noi Bai and Tan Son Nhat airports displayed or broadcast South China Sea messages, and the Vietnam Airlines website was compromised. Reports put leaked frequent-flyer records at more than 400,000 [S4][S6]. Flights were delayed as staff used manual check-in [S6].

campaigns.name: Group response to attribution (reports conflict)
campaigns.summary: A Cyware headline republishing VnExpress says the group denied involvement; other reports say it first claimed the attack and then declined to confirm or deny. The article text was not verified [S5].

campaigns.name: Bkav publishes spyware and fake-domain findings
campaigns.summary: Bkav said the malware stolen data went to xxx.dcsvn.org, a copy of the Communist Party of Vietnam website, and released a free scan tool [S4].

campaigns.name: Earth Zhulong ShellFang activity (likely related cluster)
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro verified three ShellFang loader variants used between 2020 and 2022 against telecom, technology and media targets, with GPO abuse for deployment in early 2022 [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Trend Micro publishes Earth Zhulong report
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro assessed Earth Zhulong as likely related to 1937CN; the report was first titled for Vietnam and later revised to Southeast Asian firms [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: A China-linked group using the 1937CN name; Bkav believed it was behind the 2016 intrusions [S4]. Sponsorship is not established in the sources gathered.
diamond.capability: Antivirus-disguised spyware with credential theft and remote control (2016) [S4]; macro lures, ShellFang loader and Cobalt Strike (Earth Zhulong, likely related) [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Lookalike domain dcsvn.org of the Communist Party of Vietnam site with per-victim subdomains [S4].
diamond.victim: Vietnam Airlines, Vietnamese airports, state bodies, banks, businesses, research institutes and universities [S4][S6]; telecom, technology and media firms (Earth Zhulong) [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: The 2016 airport messages concerned the South China Sea dispute [S6].
diamond.technology: Vietnamese airport public-information systems, airline web and loyalty systems, and Windows enterprise networks with Group Policy [S6][S3].

gaps: Trend Micro's Earth Zhulong report (www.trendmicro.com) could not be opened by fetch; details come from search-result summaries and secondary coverage [S1][S2][S3].

The imported leads (Recorded Future hacktivism analysis, Securityaffairs, Votiro or Sebdraven malicious-document reporting) could not be retrieved or confirmed in this pass; Votiro linkage to 1937CN and shared infrastructure is reported only second-hand.
No state sponsor, government attribution, or technical indicators (hashes, IPs) for the 1937CN-named activity were found.
Imported record says active since 2013 and mentions 2015 defacements; these were not confirmed by the sources gathered.
A secondary summary ties Earth Zhulong to the name Goblin Panda; this is unverified here and is not added as an alias.
Press reports conflict on whether the group denied or neither confirmed nor denied the airport attack [S5].
Vendor-cluster boundary: Earth Zhulong is only 'likely related' to 1937CN [S1]; no Microsoft name or MITRE group ID was found.

provenance.importedSummary: 1937CN is a Chinese hacking group that has been active since at least 2013. The group is known for targeting Vietnamese organizations, including government agencies, businesses, and media outlets. 1937CN has been linked to a number of high-profile cyberattacks, including the hacking of Vietnam Airlines in 2016 and the defacement of Vietnamese government websites in 2015.
